subject: Dedicated capacity migration playbook and burst rationale
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00Z
Subject: Dedicated capacity migration playbook and burst rationale

Team — attaching the first draft of the dedicated-capacity migration playbook for HelixHealth. This is intended to be the operational guide we hand to Ops + CS during the activation window, with the following intents: 

- Clear action owners for each activation milestone (prep, turn-up, priming, go-live)
- Autoscale & burst rationale: why we recommend 3-tier burst (reserved -> burst-on-demand -> regional overflow) and the expected cost envelope
- Regional fallback mapping: primary US-W, secondary US-E, EU for compliance-restricted traffic

Key asks: 
1) Monica — please verify the MOP timing and NetOps contacts in section 2.
2) Ben — confirm procurement gating dates with Helix (they said mid-September). If that slips we need a contingency.
3) Aditya — Ops, can you validate the autoscale thresholds and the KV-cache warmup estimates (page 8)?

Attachments: migration-playbook-v1.pdf, burst-rationale-appendix.md (short appendix with cost sims).

I plan a 30-minute sync on Tue 2026-09-01 to lock owners and finalize configs; if you have a hard blocker earlier flag here.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: R. Anderson <r.anderson@helixhealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity migration playbook and burst rationale

Thanks Karthik — quick read-through notes below (kept light so we can iterate fast):

- Section 2 (MOP): move netops contact to section 2.1 and add NetOps Pager ID. I attached the minimal staging-config snippet we use for priming to reduce ambiguity.
- Autoscale thresholds: agree with the 3-tier approach but suggest lowering the warmup target for cache-priming in prod from 15% to 10% for the first two weeks to avoid overspend during initial priming traffic.
- Fallbacks: recommend we list the explicit traffic shaper rule names that Ops will apply during cutover (helps their runbooks).

I've attached staging-config.yaml (stub) — this is what we deploy in the staging pool for smoke tests.

On procurement: Ben, can you confirm whether Helix's procurement needs a signed SOW before we schedule the turn-up window? If yes, we should gate the Tue sync until procurement confirms.

Monica
Monica Patel
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Looping in the Helix ops contact (R. Anderson) so they see the proposed timing. Quick update from procurement: Helix legal wants the final SOW and the 30-day termination clause clarified before signing. They expect to return a redline by 2026-09-08.

Operationally: Helix confirmed they can provide a short-staged traffic generator for priming, but they need us to provide the autoscale knobs and a runway estimate for burst spend. I pulled the cost sims from the burst-rationale appendix and highlighted three scenarios in the attached note (inline below).

Action items I can own:
- Get procurement confirmation on SOW redline timeline (target 9/8)
- Coordinate customer-provided priming generator plan with Karthik/Aditya (target 9/10)

If procurement slips past 9/08 we should plan a soft-launch with a reduced pool until the contract is final. Monica, can you scope the soft-launch CS coverage?

Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

----- Forwarded message -----
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-01 14:21
Subject: Cost sims (excerpt)

- Scenario A (conservative priming): Reserve 4 GPUs, burst to 8 during peak (expected incremental cost ~$2.8k/wk)
- Scenario B (aggressive priming): Reserve 6 GPUs, burst to 12 for two weeks (expected incremental cost ~$7.5k/wk)
- Scenario C (overflow safety): Reserve 4 GPUs, regional overflow to EU if US capacity exhausted (adds network egress estimates)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: R. Anderson <r.anderson@helixhealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity migration playbook and burst rationale — action owners and next steps

Thanks for the quick turn. Summary / decisions coming out of this thread: 

1) Procurement gating: Ben will own follow-up with Helix legal (target 2026-09-08). If we do not have an executed SOW by 9/10, we run the soft-launch fallback (Monica to scope).
2) Autoscale config: Aditya to validate thresholds and provide a final autoscale.json by 2026-09-07. We will adopt the conservative priming profile (Scenario A) unless Ben flags stronger customer appetite.
3) Staging & priming: Helix provides traffic generator; Ops & CS will run a 48-hour priming window before go-live and capture token-level latency/cost metrics. Karthik will publish the MOP checklist in the shared drive.

I uploaded an updated playbook with inline edits and an action-owner matrix to the shared folder below. Please add any final comments before EOD Monday so I can lock the doc for the Tue sync.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-helix-migration
HubSpot: 45372

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
